senses.definition: Of, relating to, or consisting of matter, especially physical.
examples: This compound has a number of interesting material properties.

quotes.text: the material elements of the universe

senses.definition: Of, relating to, or affecting physical well-being; corporeal; bodily.
examples: material needs

senses.definition: (logic) Of or relating to the matter of reasoning, as distinguished from the form of it, especially empirical.
examples: material cause
the material aspect of being

senses.definition: (especially law) Having real importance or great consequences; significant; substantial.
examples: found a material difference between two things
You've made several material contributions to this project.
This is the most material fact in this lawsuit.

quotes.text: discourse, which was always material, not trifling

senses.definition: Relating to or concerned with what is purely physical rather than intellectual or spiritual, especially excessively so; materialistic.
examples: the material world

senses.definition: (obsolete) Full of substance or otherwise meaning.
A basic matter (as metal, wood, plastic, fiber, etc.) from which the whole or the greater part of something physical (as a machine, tool, building, fabric, etc.) is made.
examples: Asphalt, composed of oil and sand, is a widely used material for roads.

senses.definition: (sometimes collective, preceded by a qualifying word) A person, or people collectively, who are qualified or suited for a certain position or activity.
examples: boy/girlfriend material
marriage material

senses.definition: Something (as data, observations, perceptions or ideas) that may be incorporated, elaborated or otherwise reworked into a finished form or new form, or may serve as the basis for arriving at interpretations, judgments or conclusions.
examples: teaching materials

examples: The solid materials of the mixture will settle to the bottom of the container.
